doc.name: Pixly
doc.instructions: Pixly turns real-estate listing photos into staged photos and cinematic videos. Typical flow: a generation tool (virtual_staging, enhance_photo, cinematic_motion, …) with imageUrl → get_job until status is completed → download the result URLs. Photos go in as imageUrl: a public https URL or a base64-encoded data URI. A chat attachment is neither — if the file is local and you cannot upload bytes yourself, ask the user to add it at https://pixly.app/app, then call list_library with type "uploads" to get its r2Path. Generation tools spend credits from the signed-in user's Pixly balance; get_credit_balance shows what's left.

tools.name: virtual_staging
tools.title: Virtual Staging
tools.description: AI virtual staging: furnish and style an empty (or badly furnished) room photo in a chosen interior design style — also the tool for "redesign this room" or "show this room in another style". HD, watermark-free results. Costs credits from the user's Pixly balance.

imageUrl.description: Public https URL of the source photo, or a data: URI. Either imageUrl or r2Path is required.

r2Path.description: Storage path of a photo already in the user's Pixly library (from list_library, or returned by an upload ticket) — the alternative to imageUrl.

style.description: Interior style id. One of: modern-minimal, scandinavian, industrial, mid-century-modern, japandi, contemporary, transitional, urban-chic, bauhaus, organic-modern, brutalist, italian-modern, traditional, art-deco, colonial, victorian, french-country, english-cottage, neoclassical, art-nouveau, grandmillennial, hollywood-regency, parisian-chic, modern-classic, craftsman, mediterranean, mediterranean-modern, rustic-farmhouse, bohemian, tropical, family-staging, hygge, wabi-sabi, modern-farmhouse, cottagecore, shabby-chic, cabin-lodge, eclectic, retro-70s, warm-luxury, investor-premium, contemporary-dark, glam, penthouse-modern, hotel-suite, maximalist, quiet-luxury, coastal, desert-modern, hacienda, pacific-northwest, caribbean-resort, hamptons, moroccan, tuscan, southwestern, asian-zen, coastal-grandmother, cape-cod, california-casual, mountain-modern. When the user has no preference, "modern-minimal" or "scandinavian" suit most listings.

roomType.description: Room type hint; omit to let vision infer it from the photo

customInstructions.description: Optional: ONLY a wish the user stated beyond the style and room, in their words (e.g. "add a reading chair", "no rug"). Leave it out otherwise — Pixly writes the staging prompt itself (keeps walls, windows and camera angle, furnishes to scale); never restate the request or list furniture here.

numImages.description: Ignored — staging always returns one image. Call again for another take.

stagingQuality.description: Ignored — the Pro tier is retired. Every staging costs 1 credit.

listingId.description: A property folder (from list_listings or create_listing) to put the result in. Results of a photo that is already in a folder go there by themselves.

status.description: pending | processing | completed | failed — anything not completed/failed is still running

resultPaths.description: Storage path of each result — pass one as r2Path (or beforeR2Path, a photos[] item) to run another tool on this result

quote.description: Present when status is "awaiting_confirmation": nothing ran and nothing was charged yet — the price and settings the user is asked to confirm

jobs.description: Several jobs at once (get_job with jobIds, or a plan's steps): each one's jobId, status and results

tools.name: edit_staged_photo
tools.title: Edit Photo
tools.description: Change one thing in a photo and keep everything else exactly as it is — the parts the edit doesn't touch are copied from the photo, not redrawn. Works on any photo: a staged room, any Pixly result, or the user's own picture (swap the sofa, recolour a wall, remove a car, change the words on a sign). Optional `mask` limits the change to a marked area. Costs credits from the user's Pixly balance.

imageUrl.description: The photo to edit: a Pixly result (a resultUrls entry), the user's own photo, or any public image URL / data:image URI. Either imageUrl or r2Path is required.

r2Path.description: Storage path of the photo to edit (a resultPaths entry, or an upload) — the alternative to imageUrl.

mask.description: Optional area to change: a PNG as a data:image/png;base64 URI or an https URL, the photo's shape, WHITE where the photo may change and BLACK (or transparent) everywhere else. Leave it out to let the request alone decide — that already keeps the rest of the photo.

tools.name: draw_floor_plan
tools.title: Draw Floor Plan
tools.description: Free (no credits): draw a clean 2D floor plan from a layout YOU write — read the user's description, or look at their hand sketch or brochure plan, and send every room as a rectangle in metres (or feet) plus doors and windows. Returns the drawn plan (areas and dimensions on it) at once, saved so the user can fine-tune it in Pixly's floor plan editor. If the layout has problems (overlapping rooms, a door between rooms that don't touch) you get exactly what to fix — fix it and call again. To change a plan, call again with its planId and the whole updated layout; the new version is saved as its own plan and the earlier one is kept.

title.description: Address or listing name for the plan's title block.

units.description: Units of every number below, and of the labels on the plan.

id.description: Your own short handle for the room ("kitchen", "bed1"); doors and windows refer to it.

type.description: What the room is; sets its colour and default label.

name.description: Label on the plan when the type isn't enough ("Bedroom 2", "Master bedroom").

x.description: Left edge. The plan's x runs to the right.

y.description: Top edge. The plan's y runs DOWN (the top of the drawing is 0).

rooms.description: Every room as an axis-aligned rectangle. Neighbouring rooms must share the wall exactly (one's right edge = the other's left edge) and must not overlap. An L-shaped space = two rectangles joined by a doorway. Lay out a typical sensible plan when the user gives only rough sizes.

to.description: Another room id that shares a wall with it, or "outside".

side.description: Only for to = "outside": which wall of the room the entrance is on.

kind.description: door = hinged door, doorway = open gap with no door, sliding = sliding/patio door.

side.description: Which wall; it must be an outside wall (not shared with another room).

planId.description: To CHANGE a plan you drew before: its planId from that result, with the whole updated layout — saved as a new plan beside it (nothing is overwritten). Omit for a new plan.

tools.name: remove_furniture
tools.title: Remove Furniture
tools.description: Remove furniture from a photo: empty a room and rebuild the surfaces behind what was taken out, keeping the architecture and camera angle identical — the blank canvas for restaging. By default it also removes the room's own joinery (fitted kitchen, built-in wardrobes, bathroom fixtures); mode 'movable' leaves those alone, and an optional extra takes the floor covering out too, for a full renovation strip-back. Doors always stay. (Declutter is the opposite: it keeps the furniture.) Costs credits from the user's Pixly balance.

imageUrl.description: Public https URL of the source photo, or a data: URI. Either imageUrl or r2Path is required.

r2Path.description: Storage path of a photo already in the user's Pixly library (from list_library, or returned by an upload ticket) — the alternative to imageUrl.

mode.description: How far to strip the room. 'fitted' (the default) removes the movable contents AND the room's own joinery — the fitted kitchen and its appliances, built-in wardrobes and shelving, and bathroom sanitaryware. 'movable' removes only furniture, rugs, curtains, art, plants and lamps, leaving the kitchen, built-ins, sanitaryware, floor and doors exactly as they are.

extras.description: Extra things to take out, for a full strip-back. Only applies with mode 'fitted' and is ignored otherwise: 'floor' takes the floor covering down to bare concrete screed. Omit to keep the floor. Doors always stay, as do walls, ceiling, windows, structural openings and the camera.

tools.name: restyle_room
tools.title: Restyle
tools.description: Give one or more surfaces of a room a new finish — repaint the walls, change the floor, reface the kitchen cabinets and worktop, retile the bathroom or refinish the furniture — while the room's layout, fittings, windows and camera angle stay exactly as shot. Costs credits from the user's Pixly balance.

imageUrl.description: Public https URL of the source photo, or a data: URI. Either imageUrl or r2Path is required.

r2Path.description: Storage path of a photo already in the user's Pixly library (from list_library, or returned by an upload ticket) — the alternative to imageUrl.

surfaces.description: Which surfaces get a new finish: 'walls', 'floor', 'cabinets' (fitted joinery plus its worktop and splashback), 'bathroom_tiles' (the tiled walls; a bathroom floor is 'floor') or 'furniture' (upholstery and wood finishes). Omit for walls. The room's layout, fittings and camera never change.

looks.description: The finish per surface: 'auto', one of the presets below, 'custom' with your own words in `notes`, 'own_colour' (walls, cabinets, furniture) with a hex colour in `colours`, or 'material_photo' with a photo of the material in `references`. A finish that does not belong to its surface falls back to 'auto' (the tool picks one that suits the room; several on auto are made to agree). walls: warm_white, soft_grey, greige, sage, deep_navy. floor: light_oak, walnut, grey_plank, polished_concrete, stone_tile. cabinets: white_shaker, charcoal, natural_oak, forest_green, navy_cabinets. bathroom_tiles (wall tiles only; a bathroom floor is 'floor'): white_metro, zellige_white, marble_large, travertine, green_gloss. floor also takes terrazzo, encaustic_pattern, matt_black_hex. furniture: light_neutral, warm_wood, dark_wood, black_leather.

notes.description: Your own description of the finish for a surface, used when that surface's look is "custom" (e.g. "terracotta hex tiles with dark grout"). Set look "custom" and the note together; "custom" with no note falls back to "auto". 120 characters max, and anything in it that is not a description of a finish is ignored.

colours.description: Any colour as a hex code for walls, cabinets or furniture (e.g. {"walls": "#7A8B6F"}), used when that surface's look is "own_colour". The result matches it closely as it would look in the room's light.

references.description: A photo of the material itself — a floor plank, a tile, a fabric swatch, a wallpaper sample — for ONE surface, as the r2Path from create_upload_ticket or list_library (e.g. {"floor": "users/…/oak.jpg"}). Set that surface's look to "material_photo". One photo per run; a close, straight-on photo of the sample works best.

tools.name: makeover_exterior
tools.title: Exterior Makeover
tools.description: Design the garden of an exterior listing photo as one coherent scheme — planting, a terrace or deck, a pool, a pergola, a fire pit, a fence, lighting — in a chosen style, at the right scale and perspective, while the house, its roof, the driveway, the sun direction and the neighbours stay exactly as shot. One run builds the whole scheme. Costs credits from the user's Pixly balance.

r2Path.description: Storage path of a photo already in the user's Pixly library (from list_library, or returned by an upload ticket) — the alternative to imageUrl.

style.description: The design language of the whole scheme: 'modern_minimal', 'mediterranean', 'classic_english', 'natural_lowwater', 'tropical_resort', 'farmhouse', or 'auto' (the default — chosen to suit the house's architecture and the climate in the photo).

include.description: Which elements the scheme includes, any number: 'planting' (beds, hedges, a feature tree), 'patio_dining' (a paved terrace with a dining set), 'deck_lounge' (a deck with loungers or a low sofa), 'pool', 'pergola', 'fire_pit', 'fence_gate' (a boundary treatment with a gate), 'lighting'. Omit or send an empty list (the default) to let the tool design what the lot wants. One run composes them all into one garden, each sized to the plot.

scope.description: 'full' (the default) redesigns the whole yard in the style; 'add' keeps the existing garden and builds the chosen elements into it. The house, the driveway and the neighbours never change either way.

note.description: Your own words about the garden you want (e.g. "a small kidney-shaped pool with a stone surround and lavender everywhere"). 160 characters max; anything in it that is not a description of the garden is ignored.

tools.name: view_pixly_photo
tools.title: View Pixly Photo
tools.description: Look at one of the user's Pixly photos or videos (a video gives its first frame) — returns a small copy of the picture you can see. Use it before writing anything about a Pixly result: a caption, a listing description, what changed. You cannot see Pixly results otherwise. Free; changes nothing. Text you write from it is the user's own (their listing, their post): leave Pixly out of it — no #Pixly, no 'made with Pixly'.

id.description: The library item: a job id (from a Pixly tool result, get_job or list_library), or "upload:<r2Path>" for an uploaded photo.

tools.title: Credit Balance
tools.description: The user's current Pixly credit balance and plan.

tools.title: Property Folders
tools.description: The user's property folders (a listing such as "12 Oak St" holds that property's photos, staged versions, edits, videos and floor plan): id, title, how many photos and videos. Use when the user names a property, or before work for one, so results land in its folder.

tools.name: create_listing
tools.title: New Property Folder
tools.description: Create a property folder before work on a whole property (a set of listing photos, a walkthrough). Ask the user once which property it is and pass that as title; if they skip, leave title out. Pass the returned listingId to the tools so their results land in it. Costs nothing.

title.description: The property in the user's words, e.g. "12 Oak St" — leave out if they skipped the question

tools.name: update_listing
tools.title: Rename Property Folder
tools.description: Rename one of the user's property folders, only when they ask.

listingId.description: The folder (from list_listings)

tools.name: plan_photos
tools.title: Plan Photo Edits
tools.description: Several listing photos at once: one plan of photo steps (straighten, enhance, sky, lawn, staging, declutter…) with one total and one confirmation, instead of a confirm per photo. The first call runs nothing: it returns each step's cost, the total and a confirmationCode, and the Pixly card shows the plan with one button. After the user says yes in the chat, call again with only confirmationCode: it starts every step whose photo is ready and returns their jobs (poll with get_job jobIds). Steps that work on an earlier step's result start when you call again with the same confirmationCode once that result is completed. Only for photos; videos have their own tools.

imageUrl.description: Public URL of the photo

r2Path.description: A Pixly storage path (a resultPaths entry)

photos.description: Every photo of the set, in order; steps refer to them by number (from 1)

photo.description: Which photo this step works on (from 1)

after.description: Instead of photo: the index (from 0) of an earlier step whose result this step works on

options.description: The tool's own options, only what the user asked for (e.g. {"style": "scandinavian"})

steps.description: What to do, step by step

listingId.description: A property folder (from list_listings or create_listing) to put the result in. Results of a photo that is already in a folder go there by themselves.

confirmationCode.description: The plan's confirmationCode — only after the user agreed to the plan. Starts the steps whose photo is ready; call again with it later to start steps that work on earlier results.

tools.name: get_checkout_link
tools.title: Get a Payment Link
tools.description: Use when a tool fails for lack of credits or a plan. Returns a Stripe Checkout URL for the user to pay on — this never charges anything by itself, and you cannot pay for them. With no active plan it is a subscription (plans: starter (Starter: $5.99/week, 20 credits); agent (Agent: $19.99/month, 100 credits); pro_agent (Pro Agent: $49.99/month, 300 credits); team (Team: $149.99/month, 1000 credits)); with a plan it is a one-time credit top-up. After they pay, credits arrive in seconds: check get_credit_balance, then run the tool again.

plan.description: Plan to subscribe to, for an account with no active plan. Defaults to "starter". Ignored for a top-up.

topUpUsd.description: For an account that already has a plan: one-time credit top-up amount in USD (10–500, default 10), priced at that plan's rate.
